title: Budget missing-object acquisition before searching a partial clone
applies_when: A partial clone omits source objects, or a shallow clone supplies the history for a bounded repair/ancestry investigation.
lesson: A read-looking Git command can fetch omitted objects. Before broad content search, list paths and read the pinned files needed with a timeout/acquisition budget. Supported Git versions offer --no-lazy-fetch or GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 for strictly local observations. Missing objects are incomplete evidence, not proof of absence. For an explicitly approved bounded materialization, enumerate selected blob IDs with ls-tree, batch-check their local availability, then bulk-fetch only missing IDs from the verified promisor remote. The tested Git2.53 route used fetch.negotiationAlgorithm=noop with fetch --filter=blob:none --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head --recurse-submodules=no --stdin; an ordinary blob-ID fetch failed connectivity checking before that correction. Recheck all selected blobs and use the raw-object bundler afterward. This does not authorize automatic fetch, arbitrary IDs, credentials or unbounded acquisition. Separately, shallow history stops at apparent roots even when raw commits have parents. Check --is-shallow-repository, requested history count and traversal boundary before interpreting a short log as no eligible repair. Clone depth does not guarantee that many first-parent nonmerge commits. Raw parent headers can distinguish boundary merges, but cannot recover absent ancestry. Acquire only necessary objects/history, preserve identities and charge setup cost.
avoid_when: A full build may require all relevant objects; a shallow clone can already contain the complete requested bounded frame. Do not require unshallowing every repository, impose permanent local-only gates, skip missing evidence, assume old Git supports a switch, or claim lower total cost/greater PR yield from these mechanisms. Deepening changes available history, not a frozen sample's outcomes or eligibility rule.

evidence.note: Git documents demand-fetching, bulk-prefetching and requests without packfile negotiation. This supports the mechanism behind explicitly fetching a selected missing-object batch, not every command flag, all Git/server versions or measured Scout efficiency. Partial clone limits initial acquisition, not necessarily later content operations; it is independent of shallow history.

This version documents --no-lazy-fetch and GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH, including using cat-file -e to inspect local object availability without demand-fetching. Verify availability for the actual installed Git.

Git explicitly treats shallow boundary commits as parentless for traversal although their raw commit objects have parents. This supports the incomplete-history caution, not a measured research or discovery advantage.
